info.title: TeamVault API
info.description:
API for TeamVault, the shared password manager: secrets (passwords, credit cards, files),
their payloads, shares, and revision history.

## Authentication

Every endpoint requires a bearer token (exceptions: `GET /v2/me` and
`GET /v2/password-suggestion` require a token but no scope; this documentation is public):

```
Authorization: Bearer <prefix>.<secret>
```

Tokens are issued in your TeamVault user settings (or by an administrator via the
`issue_api_token` management command) and carry **scopes**; each operation documents its
required scope. Call `GET /v2/me` to see who you are and which scopes your token holds.
Wildcard scopes (`secrets:*`) match every action on that resource. Reading decrypted
payloads requires the dedicated `secrets:data:read` scope — it is never implied by
`secrets:read` or `secrets:write`. Scopes only narrow what the token's user may already
do; they never grant access beyond the user's own permissions.

## Errors

All 4xx/5xx responses use a single envelope:

```json
{"detail": "Missing required scope: secrets:read"}
```

For validation errors (422), `detail` is a list of field-level error objects.

## Conventions for list endpoints

- **Pagination**: `?page=&page_size=` — response envelope `{count, next, previous, results}`.
  Default `page_size` is 50, maximum 200 (silently clamped).
- **Filtering**: each list endpoint documents its filter parameters. Unknown query parameters
  are rejected with 422. Multiple filters combine with AND.
- **Sorting**: `?sort=key,-key2` — comma-separated, `-` prefix for descending,
  per-endpoint allowlist of sort keys.
- **Expand**: `?expand=a,b` — opt into full objects in place of slim references,
  per-endpoint allowlist, one level deep. Unknown values are rejected with 422.

## Identifiers

Secrets and revisions are addressed by their stable `hashid` (the same identifier the
legacy `/api/` used). Users and shares are addressed by their numeric `id`; users are
never addressed by username (usernames can change).

## Migrating from the legacy DRF API

The legacy `/api/` (v1) endpoints are deprecated but frozen and still supported; every v1 response
carries RFC 8594 `Deprecation` and `Link` headers. See the migration guide at
[`/api/v2/MIGRATION.md`](/api/v2/MIGRATION.md) for the endpoint and field mapping from the
deprecated `/api/` endpoints (auth, paths, and per-resource field renames).

get.description:
Self-introspection: returns the user behind the bearer token used for this request, plus the token metadata (scopes, expiry). Useful for agents to discover which operations their token permits.

- **Required scope**: none — any valid token

Returns a freshly generated password built from the configured password-generator settings (length and minimum digits/upper/lower/special characters from the `[password_generator]` config section). The v2 home of v1's `/api/generate_password/`, now returning a `{password}` object instead of a bare string.

- **Required scope**: none — any valid token. Like `/me`, this endpoint touches no stored data (it generates a random string), so it carries no scope; the bearer token is still required.

get.description:
Lists the secrets visible to you (same visibility as the legacy `/api/`): access policy `any` and `discoverable` secrets, plus any shared directly with you; deleted secrets are excluded. Each item carries `data_readable`, telling you whether you may decrypt it.

- **Required scope**: `secrets:read`
- **Pagination**: `page`/`page_size` (default 50, max 200)
- **Filters**: `q`, `status`, `content_type`, `access_policy`, `name`, `username`, `created_by` (combine with AND)
- **Sort**: `?sort=key,-key2` with keys created_at, last_changed_at, last_read_at, name (default `name`)
- **Expand**: created_by (one level deep)
- **Related**: `get_secret`

post.description:
Creates a secret with metadata and an initial payload (`secret_data`, write-only). The shape of `secret_data` depends on `content_type` (same vocabulary as the payload-read endpoints, with `file_content` base64-encoded). The creator is automatically granted a permanent share, matching the legacy `/api/` behaviour. Returns the full secret.

- **Required scope**: `secrets:write` (does not grant `secrets:data:read`)
- **Validation**: 422 if `secret_data` does not match `content_type` (e.g. missing credit-card fields, or a file without `filename`/`file_content`)
- **Related**: `update_secret`, `get_secret`

get.description:
Returns a single secret by its `hashid`. Enforces the same access rules as the legacy `/api/`: an invisible secret returns 404, a visible-but-unreadable secret returns 403.

- **Required scope**: `secrets:read`
- **Expand**: created_by (one level deep)
- **Related**: `list_secrets`

patch.description:
Updates a secret's metadata and/or payload. Every field is optional; only provided fields change. `content_type` is immutable: sending a different value is rejected with 422. When `secret_data` is provided it is validated against the existing content type and saved as a new payload revision (re-using an existing revision when the plaintext is unchanged).

- **Required scope**: `secrets:write` (does not grant `secrets:data:read`)
- **Permissions**: an invisible secret returns 404, a visible-but-unwritable secret returns 403 (same gate as v1's update path)
- **Related**: `create_secret`, `get_secret`

delete.description:
Soft-deletes a secret: its `status` becomes `deleted` and it disappears from the default list/visibility (the row is never hard-deleted, preserving history and audit trail).

- **Required scope**: `secrets:write` (does not grant `secrets:data:read`)
- **Permissions**: an invisible secret returns 404, a visible-but-unwritable secret returns 403
- **Related**: `update_secret`

get.description:
Decrypts and returns the current payload of a secret. The response shape depends on the secret's `content_type`: a password returns `{password, otp_key_data}`, a credit card returns its card fields, and a file returns `{filename, file_content}` with the contents base64-encoded (v2 uses `file_content`, fixing v1's `file` key).

- **Required scope**: `secrets:data:read` (never implied by `secrets:read`/`secrets:write`)
- **Side effects**: Reading the payload is audited: it records the calling user in the payload's `accessed_by` set, updates `last_read`, and writes a secret-read entry to the audit log (a dedicated elevated-read category when a superuser reads a secret they only see via superuser privileges).
- **Related**: `get_secret`, `get_secret_revision_data`

Decrypts and returns the payload of a specific revision (a `SecretChange`) of a secret, identified by `revision_hashid`. Returns 404 if the revision does not belong to the given secret. The response shape matches `get_secret_data`.

- **Required scope**: `secrets:data:read` (never implied by `secrets:read`/`secrets:write`)
- **Side effects**: Reading the payload is audited: it records the calling user in the payload's `accessed_by` set, updates `last_read`, and writes a secret-read entry to the audit log (a dedicated elevated-read category when a superuser reads a secret they only see via superuser privileges).
- **Related**: `get_secret_data`

get.summary: Read a secret's current OTP token
get.description:
Computes and returns the current one-time password (TOTP) token for a password secret that has an OTP key configured. Returns 422 if the secret has no OTP key.

- **Required scope**: `secrets:data:read` (never implied by `secrets:read`/`secrets:write`)
- **Side effects**: Reading the payload is audited: it records the calling user in the payload's `accessed_by` set, updates `last_read`, and writes a secret-read entry to the audit log (a dedicated elevated-read category when a superuser reads a secret they only see via superuser privileges). The decrypted OTP key is cached in your session, so repeatedly refreshing the token within one session (cookie-retaining clients) does not multiply audit log entries.
- **Related**: `get_secret_data`

get.description:
Lists the shares of a secret: who (a user or a group) has been granted access, by whom, and until when. Each item carries a computed `is_expired`. Visibility follows the same gate as `get_secret` (an invisible secret returns 404).

- **Required scope**: `secrets:read`
- **Pagination**: `page`/`page_size` (default 50, max 200)
- **Filters**: `user`, `group`, `is_expired` (combine with AND)
- **Sort**: `?sort=key,-key2` with keys granted_at (default `-granted_at`)
- **Expand**: granted_by, group, user (one level deep)
- **Related**: `create_secret_share`, `delete_secret_share`

post.summary: Share a secret with a user or group
post.description:
Grants access to a secret to exactly one user or one group. Set exactly one of `user`/`group` (both or neither is rejected with 422). An existing active share for the same user/group is rejected (422); an expired share for the same target is replaced. Mirrors the legacy `/api/` semantics, including audit logging (a dedicated superuser category when a superuser shares a secret they only reach via superuser privileges).

- **Required scope**: `shares:write` (never implied by `secrets:write`)
- **Permissions**: you must have share access to the secret (otherwise 403)
- **Related**: `list_secret_shares`, `delete_secret_share`

delete.description:
Removes a share, revoking the granted access. Returns 404 if the share does not belong to the given secret. Mirrors the legacy `/api/` audit logging, including a dedicated superuser category when a superuser removes a share via superuser privileges.

- **Required scope**: `shares:write` (never implied by `secrets:write`)
- **Permissions**: you must have share access to the secret (otherwise 403)
- **Related**: `list_secret_shares`, `create_secret_share`

get.description:
Lists a secret's history as a chain of revisions (SecretChange rows), newest first. Each revision carries the metadata snapshot at that point in time, the actor, a `parent_hashid` linking to the previous revision, an optional `restored_from_hashid`, and a `payload` reference. Payloads are deduplicated, so several revisions may share one `payload.hashid`. Decrypted payload *content* is served separately by `get_secret_revision_data` (`secrets:data:read`). Visibility follows the same gate as `get_secret` (an invisible secret returns 404).

- **Required scope**: `secrets:read`
- **Pagination**: `page`/`page_size` (default 50, max 200)
- **Filters**: `actor`, `created_after`, `created_before` (combine with AND)
- **Sort**: `?sort=key,-key2` with keys created_at (default `-created_at`)
- **Expand**: actor (one level deep)
- **Related**: `get_secret_revision`, `get_secret_revision_data`

Returns a single revision (a SecretChange) of a secret, identified by `revision_hashid`. Returns 404 if the revision does not belong to the given secret. The shape matches an item of `list_secret_revisions`. Decrypted payload content stays behind `get_secret_revision_data` (`secrets:data:read`).

- **Required scope**: `secrets:read`
- **Expand**: actor (one level deep)
- **Related**: `list_secret_revisions`, `get_secret_revision_data`

get.description:
Lists the secrets a user must rotate when they leave: secrets that need changing (`status = needs_changing`, `needs_changing_on_leave = true`) whose current payload the user has read at some point (access-history based, so current group membership is irrelevant). The v2 home of v1's `/api/users/<username>/pending-secrets/`, addressed by numeric user id.

- **Required scope**: `users:read` — **and** the calling token must belong to a superuser (this offboarding view exposes secrets across all users; the superuser gate is the v1-parity authorization). A non-superuser token holder gets 403 even with the scope.
- **Pagination**: `page`/`page_size` (default 50, max 200)
- **Filters**: `q` (case-insensitive substring match on the secret name)
- Returns 404 for an unknown user id.

PayloadRef.description:
Slim reference to a payload (an encrypted secret revision).

A payload is the deduplicated encrypted blob behind a secret: saving the same plaintext
twice reuses one payload row, so several revisions in a secret's history may share the
same payload (and thus the same `hashid`). Decrypt the current payload via
`GET /v2/secrets/{hashid}/data`, or a historical one via
`GET /v2/secrets/{hashid}/revisions/{revision_hashid}/data`.

hashid.title: Hashid

set_by.description: The user who set this payload (model field `set_by`).

RevisionSchema.description:
One entry in a secret's history: a `SecretChange` row.

A revision captures the secret's metadata snapshot at a point in time plus a reference to the
payload (`SecretRevision`) that was current then. Payloads are deduplicated, so several
revisions may share one `payload.hashid` (e.g. after a restore or a metadata-only edit). The
decrypted payload content is never part of this resource; fetch it via
`GET /v2/secrets/{hashid}/revisions/{revision_hashid}/data` (requires `secrets:data:read`).

hashid.description: Stable identifier of the revision (the SecretChange hashid). Use it at the `/revisions/{revision_hashid}/data` endpoint to decrypt this revision.
hashid.title: Hashid

created_at.description: When this revision was recorded (model field `created`).
created_at.title: Created At

actor.description: The user who made this change. Slim reference by default; full User with ?expand=actor.
actor.title: Actor

parent_hashid.description: Hashid of the previous revision in the linear history chain (model field `parent`), or null for the first revision.
parent_hashid.title: Parent Hashid

restored_from_hashid.description: If this revision was created by restoring an earlier one, the hashid of that source revision (model field `restored_from`); otherwise null.
restored_from_hashid.title: Restored From Hashid

payload.description: Reference to the payload that was current at this revision (model field `revision`). Payloads are deduplicated, so several revisions may share one payload hashid.

examples: Read-write credentials for the prod cluster.
description.title: Description

filename.description: Secret filename at this revision (file secrets only).
filename.title: Filename

access_policy.description: Access policy at this revision. One of 'any', 'discoverable', 'hidden'.
access_policy.title: Access Policy

status.description: Lifecycle status at this revision. One of 'ok', 'needs_changing', 'deleted'.
status.title: Status

needs_changing_on_leave.description: Whether the secret required rotation on leave at this revision.
needs_changing_on_leave.title: Needs Changing On Leave

scrubbed_at.description: When this revision had its metadata scrubbed by a superuser, or null if it was never scrubbed. When set, the snapshot fields above reflect the post-scrub state.
scrubbed_at.title: Scrubbed At

scrubbed_by.description: The superuser who scrubbed this revision, or null if it was never scrubbed.

RevisionSchema.title: RevisionSchema

q.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the secret name.
q.title: Q

count.description: Total number of items across all pages.
count.title: Count

next.description: Absolute URL of the next page, or null on the last page.
next.title: Next

previous.description: Absolute URL of the previous page, or null on the first page.
previous.title: Previous

PendingSecret.description: A secret a user must rotate on leaving: it needs changing and the user has read it.

hashid.description: Stable identifier of the secret (the same identifier the legacy `/api/` used).
hashid.title: Hashid

status.description: Secret status, always 'needs_changing' for a pending secret.
status.title: Status

web_url.description: Absolute URL of the secret in the TeamVault web UI.
web_url.title: Web Url

last_changed_at.description: When the secret was last changed (v1 `last_changed`).
last_changed_at.title: Last Changed At

last_read_at.description: When the secret was last read by anyone (v1 `last_read`).
last_read_at.title: Last Read At

last_shared.description: When the secret was most recently shared (max of its shares' `granted_on`); null if never.
last_shared.title: Last Shared

PendingSecret.title: PendingSecret
